title: Bounded coherent upper shriek for perfect finite-type maps
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to A$ be a finite-type homomorphism of commutative Noetherian rings such that $A$ is perfect over a polynomial presentation of $\varphi$, and let $\varphi^!:D(R)\to D(A)$ be the algebraic upper-shriek functor of [lem-trf-algebraic-shriek-calculus]. Then $\varphi^!$ sends complexes with bounded finitely generated cohomology over $R$ to complexes with bounded finitely generated cohomology over $A$. In particular, $\varphi^!(R[0])$ has bounded finitely generated cohomology over $A$.

source.place: Tag 0BZK, lemma-shriek-boundedness, parts (1)(2): a perfect finite-type map preserves bounded coherent complexes under upper shriek.

proof.text: Fix any $K\in D(R)$ with bounded finitely generated cohomology. Choose the polynomial presentation $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ in the hypothesis. The variables generate $P$ over $R$, so the finite-type Noetherian-algebra theorem makes $P$ Noetherian. By perfectness choose a finite-projective $P$-complex $E$ with $Q_PE\cong A[0]$ and integers $u\le v$ such that $E^i=0$ outside $[u,v]$; for the zero complex choose $u=v=0$. The algebraic shriek calculus identifies restriction of $\varphi^!K$ along $P\to A$ with $R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P)[n]$ in $D(P)$.

source.place: Tag 0BZK, lemma-shriek-boundedness (2), polynomial extension and reflection under restriction of scalars; Tag 0BZI for the polynomial shriek model.

proof.text: Apply the polynomial bounded finite model lemma to this bounded finite-cohomology $K\in D(R)$. It supplies a bounded complex $G$ of finite $P$-modules, supported in some $[a,b]$, and an isomorphism $Q_PG\cong K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P$ in $D(P)$. This does not require $K$ to be perfect.

source.place: Tag 0BZK, lemma-shriek-boundedness (2), polynomial extension and reflection under restriction of scalars; Tag 0BZI for the polynomial shriek model.

proof.text: Apply the finite-projective Hom coherent-model lemma over the Noetherian ring $P$ to $E,G$. It gives $C=\operatorname{Hom}_P^\bullet(E,G)$ with finite terms, support in $[a-v,b-u]$, finite cohomology, and $Q_PC\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_P(Q_PE,Q_PG)$. Write $\alpha:Q_PE\cong A[0]$ and $\beta:Q_PG\cong K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P$ for the chosen isomorphisms. The derived-Hom functor sends $(\alpha^{-1},\beta)$ to an isomorphism from this Hom object to $R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P)$. Compose it with the model comparison and shift by $[n]$: step 1 then identifies restriction of $\varphi^!K$ with $Q_P(C[n])$.

source.place: Tag 0BZK, lemma-shriek-boundedness (2), polynomial extension and reflection under restriction of scalars; Tag 0BZI for the polynomial shriek model.

proof.text: Restriction of scalars from $A$ to $P$ computes kernels, images and quotients on the same underlying abelian groups, hence also cohomology. With the cohomological shift convention $(C[n])^t=C^{t+n}$, its degree-$t$ cohomology is $H^{t+n}(C)$. It vanishes unless $a-v\le t+n\le b-u$, equivalently $a-v-n\le t\le b-u-n$, and is finite over $P$. For each $t$, transport a finite set of $P$-generators through this cohomology isomorphism. Every expression $\sum p_jm_j$ equals the $A$-linear expression $\sum\overline{p_j}m_j$, since the action factors through $P\to A$. These generators therefore generate $H^t(\varphi^!K)$ over $A$, proving the first assertion.

source.place: Tag 0BZK, lemma-shriek-boundedness (2), polynomial extension and reflection under restriction of scalars; Tag 0BZI for the polynomial shriek model.

proof.text: Take $K=R[0]$. Its cohomology is zero outside degree zero and is generated by $1$ in degree zero (the zero ring is included). The result just proved gives bounded finitely generated $A$-cohomology for $\varphi^!(R[0])$.

source.place: Tag 0BZK, lemma-shriek-boundedness (2), polynomial extension and reflection under restriction of scalars; Tag 0BZI for the polynomial shriek model.
